Jalla Saidulu And 2 Others vs Thumoz Hari Prasad And Another
on 12 August, 2024
 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 M.A.C.M.A Nos.2099 of 2013 and 2968 of 2016
Common Judgment

entities.text: Jalla Saidulu And 2 Others vs Thumoz Hari Prasad And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
:
Aggrieved by the award dated 17.07.2013 in O.P.No.434 of 2012 passed by the III Additional District Judge (I Fast Track Court) at Nalgonda, the claimants have filed MACMA No.2968 of 2016 for enhancement of the compensation and the Insurance Company has filed MACMA No.2099 of 2013 questioning the quantum of compensation.
2.

entities.text: III Additional District Judge (I Fast Track Court) at Nalgonda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Since both the appeals arise out of the very same finding in O.P.No.434 of 2012, both the appeals are disposed of by way of common judgment.
3. Having heard Sri P.Ramakrishna Reddy, learned counsel for the claimants, Sri B.Narayana Reddy, learned counsel for the Insurance Company, perused the entire material on record.
4. The manner of accident and the death of the deceased are not disputed by either of the parties.
5. The claimant Nos.1 and 2 are the sons of the deceased and claimant No.3 is the daughter of the deceased.

They have filed the claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- and the Tribunal has granted Rs.2,84,000/- directing the respondent Nos.1 and 2 to deposit the amount.
6.

According to version of the claimants, on 24.03.2012 at 05.30 am, while the deceased and her son were crossing the road at the outskirts of Aakupamula village to go to Nalgonda town, meantime the offending vehicle which is Ambulance bearing No.AP 29 TA 7205 proceedings towards Kodad side drove the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and hit the deceased.
Due to which, the deceased sustained severe injuries to head and all over the body and died on the spot.

7. Learned counsel for the claimant would submit that though the deceased was doing kirana business and earning an amount of Rs.5000/- per month, the Tribunal considering the income at Rs.3000/- per month granted compensation accordingly.
Learned counsel requested the Court to consider the income at Rs.4,500/- per month and grant compensation.
8. Having gone through the evidence on record, the learned Tribunal has rightly concluded that the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
9. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company would submit that the claimants would not depend on the mother and accordingly the reduction of income should be at 50% and not 1/3rd.
Admittedly, the Hon'ble Supreme Court as laid down the conditions that only in the event of bachelor the income would be deducted at 50%.
Here, the deceased was the mother and in fact she Jalla Saidulu And 2 Others vs Thumoz Hari Prasad And Another on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110012846/

entities.text: Jalla Saidulu And 2 Others vs Thumoz Hari Prasad And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 was housewife and also doing kirana business.
In the said circumstances, even assuming that the children are not dependent, however, the reduction of income should be at 1/3rd only.

10. This Court relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Ramachandrappa Vs.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance 1, where the monthly income of the daily wage labourer is considered at Rs.4,500/- without there being any evidence, is inclined to take the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- as claimed by the claimants.

entities.text:
Ramachandrappa Vs.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. The Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi2 has held that while considering the compensation in cases of death, the future prospects of the self employed shall also be considered.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having regard to the age of deceased i.e. 51 years as on the date of accident and occupation as self-employed, if 10% (percent) of the income is included as future prospects, the annual income would come to Rs.59,400/- (Rs.4500+450x12).

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Smt. Sarla Varma v Delhi Transport Corporation 3, since the dependants are three members, if 1/3rd of 1 (2011) 13 SCC 236 2 2017 (6) 170 (SC) 3 2009(6) SCC 121 the income is deducted towards personal expenditure, the annual contribution of the deceased to the claimants would be Rs.39,600/- (Rs.59,400-19,800).

entities.text: Smt. Sarla Varma v Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Schedule II of the Act, the relevant multiplier for the age of the deceased is '11'.
Thus, the compensation under the head of loss of dependency comes to Rs.4,35,600/- (Rs.39,600 X 11).
12. As regards the consortium to be paid, each claimant is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards consortium as decided by the Hon'ble Apex court in case of Pranay Sethi (1 Supra).
With regard to the funeral expenses and loss of estate, the claimants are entitled for Rs.30,000/-.

13. Therefore, the claimants/appellants are eligible for the compensation as below:
 Head Compensation awarded  (1) Loss of dependency Rs.4,35,600/-
 (2) Funeral expenses and Rs.30,000  Loss of Estate  (3) Loss of parental consortium Rs.40,000 for claimant Nos.1  to 3  Total compensation awarded Rs.5,05,600/-
14.
In the result, the Motor Accident Miscellaneous Appeal of the Insurance Company fails and the same is dismissed.

However, the Motor Accident Miscellaneous Appeal of the claimants are allowed enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.2,84,000/- to Rs.5,05,600/-
as hereunder:

2 (a) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.

(c) The Respondent Nos.1 and 2 shall deposit the amount within a period of (8)
weeks from the date of receipt of copy of judgment.
On such deposit, claimants are permitted to withdraw entire amount without furnishing any security.
(d) Amounts shall be apportioned in terms of the ratio decided by the Tribunal in the Award.

Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
